arXiv:2611.04115v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wormlike micellar solutions exhibit formulation-dependent nonlinear startup responses, including stress overshoot, undershoot, and strain hardening, making prediction across compositions and shear rates challenging. We developed a multi-fidelity machine-learning framework to predict stress-growth curves in cetylpyridinium chloride (CPyCl)-based wormlike micelles from sparse experimental measurements. The framework combines a low-fidelity analytical model describing the overall startup response with high-fidelity experimental data capturing formulation-specific nonlinear features. item.title: Ermakov--Based embeddings as a parameter-free layer for physics-informed neural networks
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Roberto Bernal-Jaquez, Roberto Romero Huerta, Alexander Schaum
arXiv:2611.03964v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Evolution equations with time-dependent coefficients force a neural solver to spend capacity on a scale that the equation already determines. We show that a single classical object, the Ermakov-Pinney scale function h̊o, can be written into the input layer of a physics-informed neural network as a parameter-free embedding. One construction covers three problem families through the two signs of the Pinney constant c: linear diffusion (c=-1, ømegaequiv0), diffusion in a time-dependent confining trap (c=-1, ømega≠0), and the quantum oscillator with time-dependent frequency (c=+1). An exact moment identity gives h̊o in closed form from the initial data alone, so no auxiliary network or knowledge of the solution is needed. Our central finding is…

arXiv:2611.04270v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inferring upper-ocean velocity from altimetric sea surface height (SSH) remains challenging below 50~km, scales now resolved by the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission. item.title: Toward Intelligent Thermal Fluids: AI-Driven Design of Zeta-Engineered Nanofluids and Self-Organized Thermal Transport Networks
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Zhong Hu, Haiping Hong
The development of next-generation nanofluids requires a shift from empirical formulation approaches toward data-driven design strategies that simultaneously optimize thermal conductivity, dynamic viscosity, stability, and system-level performance. This perspective highlights the emerging convergence of artificial intelligence (AI), zeta-potential (ZP) engineering, and advanced nanomaterials for the design of intelligent thermal fluids. Particular emphasis is placed on ZP-engineered nanofluids, in which electrostatic interactions are deliberately tailored to control nanoparticle dispersion, stability, and the formation of self-organized thermal transport networks. item.description:

👤 Qing-Yu Li, Zhen Zheng
arXiv:2611.04214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the superfluid phases of a two-dimensional degenerate Fermi gas in an optical lattice subject to a dₓy-wave altermagnetic term that couples to the in-plane spin component. The single-particle Hamiltonian generates anisotropic Fermi surfaces for the two pseudo-spin species while maintaining zero net polarization. Using the Bogoliubov-de Gennes approach, we show that this anisotropy favors Cooper pairing at a finite center-of-mass momentum, producing a competition between Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) and Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov (FFLO) pairing and leading to FFLO superfluids. arXiv:2611.04347v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose an altermagnetism-induced route to a two-dimensional higher-order topological Dirac semimetal in a trilayer nonsymmorphic Dirac system. Interlayer hybridization preserves the nonsymmorphic bulk Dirac crossings and generates helical edge states in the trilayer phase. Introducing outer-layer d-wave altermagnetic order gaps the helical edge states, while only the symmetry-protected Dirac crossing at high-symmetry point M remains gapless. The resulting phase hosts a surviving bulk Dirac point, gapped edge spectra, and corner states. An exact layer-space decomposition further reveals that these features arise from the coexistence of a gapless Dirac sector and a gapped Z₂ topological sector. arXiv:2611.03670v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A defining feature of quantum materials is that multiple orders govern low-energy physics and are not independent. We study Bi₂Se₃ by combining DFT with a renormalized correlated honeycomb model in which frustrated magnetic order and helical topological surface states are coupled via one control parameter. The surface states map to a honeycomb Hubbard model with frustrated J₁₋₋J₂ exchange. Exact diagonalization up to 20 sites shows the Néel structure factor and valence-bond-solid order parameter cross at J₂/J₁ approx 0.22, agreeing with QMC/DMRG, and a dynamical spin structure factor broadens near the crossover, as expected for a spinon continuum. arXiv:2611.04729v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The real mechanism of ferromagnetism in III-V diluted magnetic semiconductors such as Ga₁₋ₓMnₓAs is still debated. The experimental results point out the realization of appreciable ferromagnetism at filling of the impurity band close to one-half that can be expressed in terms of compensation degree. Based on our recent results on the existence of two competing mechanisms of pair indirect exchange (with ferro- and antiferro alignment of Mn d shells), a theory of magnetic ordering in (Ga,Mn)As is presented. The molecular-field-like equation is derived in which the effective exchange constant contains all necessary information about material, including the Mn content, the compensation degree, the crystal coordination, and the parameters of two…

item.title: Engineering Fractional Topological Superconductors: Numerical Bogoliubov-de Gennes Analysis for Parafermion Realization in FCI-Superconductor Heterostructures
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Aaron Amire
arXiv:2512.16025v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a pathway to engineer Z3 parafermion zero modes in fractional Chern insulator-superconductor heterostructures. Using numerical Bogoliubov-de Gennes calculations and edge-theory analysis, we demonstrate how realistic materials such as MoTe2/NbSe2 can host parafermionic excitations with experimentally accessible signatures, including fractional Josephson effects, localized zero modes, interferometry, and thermal transport. Our work outlines concrete strategies for experimentally accessing parafermionic excitations in FCI-superconductor heterostructures.

arXiv:2611.04050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neutron scattering provides microscopic information on magnetic order and spin dynamics. Longitudinal polarization analysis (LPA), established in the pioneering work of Moon, Riste, and Koehler at Oak Ridge National Laboratory in the late 1960s, separates magnetic and nonmagnetic scattering contributions through their different effects on the neutron spin. item.title: Small-data physics-informed ML model for magnetic exchange based on chemical composition and structure
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Brice Kengni Zanguim, Thibaut Véry, Marie-Bernadette Lepetit
arXiv:2611.04681v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we propose an ensemble model based on a swarm of dense neural networks, able to predict Heisenberg exchange interactions within less than 1% error. The model uses the inputs of the ab-initio Schrödinger equation, i.e. the compound structure and chemical composition. In this first work, we trained the model on a few compounds of the hexagonal manganite family and were able to infer, with similar accuracy, the J values for other compounds of the same family at randomly chosen geometries, thus showing that we accurately learned the effect of the chemical composition and structure on effective magnetic integrals J.

item.title: Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics Reveals Grotthuss Transport in Concentrated Electrolytes
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Øystein Gullbrekken, Sondre Kvalvåg Schnell
arXiv:2611.04558v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Proton transfer is responsible for the anomalous high conductivity in acidic or basic aqueous solutions. Yet, the contribution of the proton transfer mechanism to the conductivity of concentrated aqueous solutions is unknown. In this work, we compute the transport properties of KOH(aq) systems with different concentrations, using Molecular Dynamics simulations with a Machine Learning Interatomic Potential (MLIP), which includes proton transfer. We quantify the contribution of the proton transfer mechanism to the diffusivities of hydroxide ions and water molecules, and the ionic conductivity and transport numbers of the electrolytes. The contribution is substantial at lower concentrations, but diminishes at very high concentrations.

item.title: An example of universal braiding in Links--Gould topological quantum computation
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Matthew Harper, Ben-Michael Kohli
arXiv:2611.04290v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a universal quantum computational encoding via braiding in Links--Gould fusion spaces associated to U_q^H(mathfraksl(2|1)) where q is on the unit circle and is not a root of unity. The construction uses only neglectons and is realized in the morphism spaces HomU_q^H(V(0,α),V(0,-frac12)øtⁱmes ²Nøtimes V(0,α)). Under explicit positivity and arithmetic constraints these spaces admit a 2^N-dimensional computational subspace with a positive definite Hermitian form. We prove single-qubit density in U(2,1) and approximate arbitrary unitary operators on N-qubit computational subspaces with arbitrarily small leakage. The calculations use explicit inclusions, projections, and Hermitian pairings without requiring F-matrices.
